speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and weakness in your upper limbs. To help me determine the cause, could you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if they are getting worse?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest, along with diplopia on vertical gaze, strongly suggests a neuromuscular junction issue. REQUEST TEST: Anti-AChR antibodies. REQUEST TEST: Repetitive nerve stimulation. Do you notice any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty swallowing?

The clinical picture of fatigable weakness that worsens with activity and improves with rest, combined with vertical diplopia, is classic for this condition.
